The agreement is reviewed with the regional office for the required form and content.
Updating: The Administrator reviews the agreement at least annually and when providers change, and keeps a current copy in the facility file.

Pre-admission screening: At the pre-admission evaluation (AD-02), the Case Manager records any history of mental illness, current treatment, medications and prior crises. The Case Manager obtains the applicant's consent to speak with treating providers.
Admission decision: If screening shows possible danger to self or others, the Administrator decides on admission under AD-01 and documents the reasons.

Referral: When staff observe signs of a mental health need or a resident asks for help, they report to the Case Manager the same day. The Case Manager makes a referral to [MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDER] or to the resident's chosen provider within [2] business days, and sooner if urgent.

ISP entries: The Case Manager records in the ISP (AD-03) the diagnosis if known, treatment providers, appointment schedule, medications, triggers and warning signs, and a crisis plan with names and phone numbers.

Appointments and support: Staff arrange transportation and reminders for appointments (see OPT-01). The Case Manager obtains follow-up information after each visit, within the limits of the resident's consent and confidentiality (RS-07).
Medication coordination: Changes to psychiatric medications are made only on a physician's or prescriber's written order. Staff follow MED-01 and MED-02 for storage and assistance.

Monitoring: The Case Manager checks on residents with mental health needs at least [monthly], and more often as the ISP states. The Case Manager documents mood, behavior, appointment attendance and any concerns in the ISP.

Crisis response: In an emergency, staff stay with the resident and follow the crisis plan. They call 911 if there is imminent danger and notify the Administrator, the provider and the resident's representative. Reports follow SAF-02, and RS-04 applies to any hospital transfer.
Suicide attempt: A suicide attempt is treated as an emergency and reported as an incident under SAF-02. The Administrator reviews the ISP, the supervision level and the mental health agreement steps.
Retention review: If a resident's condition may no longer be safely managed in the home, the Administrator begins the review in AD-06 and documents the steps taken.
Staff training: Staff are oriented on recognizing mental health crises, de-escalation and these procedures at orientation (ORI-01) and in annual in-service (ORI-02).
Annual review: The Administrator reviews referral timeliness and crisis events through the quality assurance process in GOV-02.

responsibilities.duty: Signs and maintains the mental health services agreement, confirms its form with the regional office, decides admission and retention questions and reviews crisis events.
Screens, refers, coordinates with providers, records contacts and the crisis plan in the ISP, and monitors.
Observe and report changes, follow the crisis plan, assist with medications within their authority and call for emergency help when needed.

documentation: Signed mental health services agreement and annual review notes
Pre-admission screening notes and consents to contact providers
Referral log with dates and outcomes
ISP entries: providers, appointments, medications, crisis plan
Monitoring notes and appointment follow-up
Incident reports for any crisis or suicide attempt

policies.title: Disaster and Emergency Plan, Evacuation and DOH Notifications
policies.applies_to: All staff, residents and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME]; Administrator, employee in charge, Case Manager and maintenance staff
policies.purpose: To maintain a written, DOH-approved plan that protects residents during fires, severe weather, utility failures, loss of essential services and other emergencies, including evacuation, and to ensure that DOH is notified on time.
policies.policy:
This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 10 - Disaster and Emergency Plan: submit a copy of the disaster and emergency plan, including evacuation procedures.

[AGENCY NAME] maintains a written disaster and emergency plan, approved by DOH under 18 NYCRR 487.12, and a copy is submitted with the Part II application (18 NYCRR 485.6). The plan includes evacuation procedures. It addresses residents with mobility, cognitive and sensory needs, and the home complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101) in planning for residents with disabilities.

The plan is reviewed at least annually and after each event or drill that exposes a weakness. The home notifies DOH by the next business day of a work stoppage, a fire, loss of a fire system, loss of hot water or loss of essential services. The home keeps an account on the Health Commerce System (HPN) with 24/7 contacts and updates it monthly. Fire safety, drills and evacuation drills are detailed in EM-02.

definitions.definition: The written DOH-approved plan describing how the home will respond to fires, severe weather, utility loss, evacuation and other emergencies.
The DOH secure web system on which the home maintains its account and 24/7 emergency contacts.
Services needed for resident health and safety, such as heat, hot water, electricity, water, fire protection systems, food and staffing.
Moving residents from danger, either partially (to a safe area within the building) or totally (out of the building).
The staff member responsible for the home during a shift, who directs the first response (see STF-01).

procedures: Plan development: Before opening, the Administrator prepares the written plan. It covers fire, severe weather, power and water loss, heat or cooling failure, loss of fire protection, bomb or security threat, medical emergency with many residents, work stoppage, infectious disease outbreaks and evacuation.

Evacuation content: The plan identifies exits and routes, primary and alternate relocation sites with written agreements with [RELOCATION SITE], transportation, a roster and medication and record transfer, and ways to account for every resident.

Special needs: The plan lists residents who need help with mobility, cognitive or sensory impairment, oxygen or other equipment, and states the staff and equipment assigned to each. The Case Manager updates the list each month and whenever the ISP changes (AD-03).

DOH approval: The Administrator submits the plan to DOH with Part II (18 NYCRR 485.6) and corrects it as the regional office requires. The approved version is kept at [LOCATION] and is available to every shift.
Staff training: The Administrator teaches the plan to all new staff at orientation (ORI-01) and to all staff at least annually (ORI-02). Each staff member signs that training was completed.
Posting: Evacuation maps and emergency contact numbers are posted at [LOCATIONS]. Residents are oriented to them at admission and after any change.
Emergency response: In an emergency, the employee in charge calls 911 first if life is in danger, starts the plan, assigns staff, protects residents and notifies the Administrator immediately.

Accounting for residents: During and after any evacuation, staff use the current roster to account for every resident, and record the location of each. The employee in charge reports any missing resident under SAF-02.

DOH notification: By the next business day the Administrator notifies the DOH regional office of any work stoppage, fire, loss of a fire system, no hot water or loss of essential services. The Administrator records the date, time, person contacted and information given. Regional offices: Capital (518) 408-5287; Central (315) 477-8472; Western (585) 423-8188; Metropolitan (212) 417-4440. The home uses the office for its region at [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE].

Other reporting: Events that are also reportable incidents are reported under SAF-02 and REC-02. Residents' families and representatives are informed promptly of any evacuation or danger to a resident.
HPN account: The Administrator keeps an active HPN account with 24/7 contact names and numbers, and the Administrator or designee reviews and updates it monthly, recording the date.

Utility and service failure: Maintenance staff keep emergency numbers for [UTILITY COMPANY], [FIRE ALARM SERVICE AGENCY] and [PLUMBER/HVAC]. They report any loss of essential services to the Administrator at once, and the Administrator arranges alternate food, water, heat and medication storage as needed.
Supplies: The home keeps emergency supplies of [water, flashlights, batteries, first aid, resident roster, medications list] as listed in the plan. The Administrator checks them [quarterly].

Medications and records in an evacuation: The nurse or medication staff take the current medication supply and records, following MED-01 and MED-02, and the employee in charge takes the roster, ISP summaries and contact lists.

Return and recovery: After an emergency, the Administrator checks safety with the authorities, returns residents when the home is safe and checks each resident's condition and any needed physician contact (RS-04).

Review: Within [14] days of any event, and at least once a year, the Administrator reviews the plan with staff and revises it where needed. If the revision changes evacuation procedures, the revised plan is sent to the regional office.
Quality assurance: Event reviews and plan updates are reported through GOV-02.

responsibilities.duty: Writes, updates and submits the plan, trains staff, notifies DOH by the next business day, and maintains the HPN account monthly.
Directs the first response, accounts for residents and notifies the Administrator.
Keeps the special-needs list current and helps residents during evacuations.
Check emergency equipment and utilities, and report failures at once.
Know the plan, take part in drills and follow instructions in an emergency.

documentation: Current DOH-approved written disaster and emergency plan, with evacuation procedures
Staff training and orientation sign-in sheets
Special-needs resident list with monthly updates
DOH notification log (date, time, event, person contacted)
HPN account monthly update record
Relocation site agreements
Post-event review reports and plan revisions

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
policies.applies_to: All staff, residents and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME]; Administrator, employee in charge, maintenance staff
policies.purpose: To prepare staff and residents to respond safely to fire through regular drills, required evacuation practice, annual outside observation, complete records and a sprinklered building.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will conduct fire drills as required by 18 NYCRR 487.12. Staff fire drills are held monthly, at varied times, and include full and partial evacuation. Drills that include residents are held quarterly, and one total evacuation is held every 12 months. Once a year, a resident drill is observed by the fire authorities, a certified service agency or DOH. The home keeps a record of every drill.

The building is protected by sprinklers throughout, as required for buildings of 25 or more beds by 18 NYCRR 487.11. The home also keeps fire protection and alarm systems and the call system working, in accordance with that section. Loss of a fire system is reported to DOH by the next business day under EM-01.

definitions.definition: A drill, held monthly at varied times, in which staff practice the fire response and full and partial evacuation.
A drill held quarterly in which residents take part.
A drill, held once every 12 months, in which all residents are moved out of the building.
Moving residents from the area of danger to a safe area of the building.
An outside agency qualified to observe resident drills, as permitted by 18 NYCRR 487.12.

procedures: Schedule: At the start of each year the Administrator prepares a drill schedule covering all 12 monthly staff drills, 4 quarterly resident drills, the annual total evacuation and the annual outside observation. The schedule is varied across days, shifts (including nights and weekends) and times.

Monthly staff drill: The employee in charge, or the Administrator, conducts a staff fire drill every month at a time that differs from the previous month. Over the year, drills cover each shift. Each drill includes full and partial evacuation practice.

Quarterly resident drill: Once each quarter, a drill with residents is held. Staff assist residents according to the special-needs list (EM-01), with additional help for residents who have mobility, cognitive or sensory needs.
Total evacuation: At least once every 12 months, the home conducts a total evacuation of all residents to the designated assembly area, and times it.

Annual observation: The Administrator arranges for the local fire authorities, a certified service agency or DOH to observe a resident drill once a year. The Administrator books the date at least [30] days ahead and records the observer's name and any recommendations.

Drill conduct: During each drill, the person in charge announces the drill, activates the alarm as appropriate, checks that staff close doors, take the roster, move residents by the planned routes and account for each person at the assembly area.

Record: Immediately afterwards, the person in charge completes the drill record: date, time, shift, type (staff, resident, total evacuation), full or partial evacuation, number of staff and residents participating, evacuation time, problems and who conducted the drill. The Administrator reviews and signs it within [3] business days.

Problem correction: Any problem found, such as blocked exits, slow evacuation or a staff member not knowing the plan, is assigned to a named person with a due date. The Administrator retrains staff and may repeat the drill.

Orientation: New staff are taught fire procedures, extinguisher use, alarm locations and exits before working alone (ORI-01). Residents are oriented to exits and procedures within [7] days of admission.

Sprinklers and fire systems: The Administrator ensures that the sprinkler system, fire alarm system and call system are inspected and maintained by [FIRE PROTECTION SERVICE AGENCY]. Maintenance staff check exits, extinguishers and alarm panels [weekly] and log the results.

System loss: If a fire system, sprinkler or alarm is out of service, the employee in charge notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator arranges repair, starts interim safety measures such as a fire watch, and notifies DOH by the next business day (EM-01).

Actual fire: In an actual fire, staff follow the emergency steps in EM-01: sound the alarm, call 911, rescue residents from immediate danger, close doors, evacuate and account for all residents. The event is reported under SAF-02.
Records retention: Drill records and inspection reports are kept at [LOCATION] and retained under REC-01, and are available to surveyors.
Annual review: The Administrator reviews all drill results at least once a year and reports through GOV-02.

responsibilities.duty: Schedules and ensures all required drills, arranges the annual observation, reviews drill records and ensures fire systems are maintained and failures are reported.
Conducts drills as assigned, directs evacuation, and completes the drill record.
Inspect exits, extinguishers and alarm equipment, and report problems.
Take part in drills, know exits and assist residents.

documentation: Annual drill schedule
Monthly staff drill records, with varied times
Quarterly resident drill records
Annual total evacuation record
Annual observation report from fire authorities, certified service agency or DOH
Fire system inspection, test and repair records
Corrective action notes and staff training records

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, nurse or designated health professional, medication-authorized staff, Case Manager
policies.purpose: To make sure that medications are managed safely: residents who can self-administer are supported, staff assistance stays within legal limits, medications are stored securely, and no dose changes are made without physician authorization.
policies.policy:
This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 11 - Medication Management Policies and Procedures.

Medication management at [AGENCY NAME] follows 18 NYCRR 487.7(f) for adult homes and 18 NYCRR 488.7(d) for enriched housing, as 10 NYCRR 1001.10 requires for assisted living residences. Residents may self-administer medications when they are able. Staff assistance is limited to what the regulations allow, is given only by authorized staff (see MED-02), and is recorded in the medication assistance record. Medications are stored securely. Staff may not give injections, except licensed staff acting within their scope. Medication doses are never changed without physician authorization.

Before the regional office's on-site inspection, the Administrator will apply for a Class 3A limited controlled substance license, as the application requires. Controlled substances will be handled in accordance with State controlled substance regulations. The Administrator will confirm the applicable text with the regional office and the licensing authority and will update this policy before opening. Who may assist, staff authorization, the assistance record and PRN rules are in MED-02.

definitions.definition: A resident taking his or her own medication independently, with or without reminders.
Limited help by authorized staff, within the limits of 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d) and 10 NYCRR 1001.10, such as handing a resident the container, as detailed in MED-02.
A medication ordered 'as needed', which is given only according to the physician's written order and the rules in MED-02.
A drug regulated under State controlled substance law, which requires added storage and record controls and a Class 3A limited license.
The limited controlled substance license the home must obtain before the regional office's on-site inspection.

procedures: Class 3A license: The Administrator submits the Class 3A limited controlled substance license application before the regional office's on-site inspection. The Administrator keeps the license and any conditions on file and renews it as required.

Assessment: At the pre-admission evaluation and at each reassessment (AD-02, AD-03), the Case Manager and nurse or designated health professional determine whether the resident can self-administer safely. They review the physician's evaluation (DSS-3122) and record the finding and any assistance needed in the ISP.

Self-administering residents: A resident who self-administers keeps medications in the room only if secured in a locked space the resident controls and the assessment says it is safe. Staff check the supply and the resident's ability at least [monthly] and record the check. If a resident is no longer able to self-administer, the ISP is updated.

Orders: Staff accept medications only with a current written physician or authorized prescriber order. The nurse or designated person checks the order against the medication label and the medication list, and clarifies any difference with the prescriber before use.

Staff assistance: Only staff authorized under MED-02 may assist residents, and only within the limits of 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d) and 10 NYCRR 1001.10. Staff do not give injections, except licensed staff within their scope, and do not perform tasks beyond their authorization.

No changes without orders: Staff never change, skip, double or substitute doses, or crush or alter medications, without written physician authorization. If a resident refuses or a dose is missed, staff record it and notify the nurse and the physician as ordered.

Medication assistance record: Each time staff assist, they record the medication, dose, time and initials in the medication assistance record, as MED-02 states. PRN use includes the reason and result.

Secure storage: All medications kept by the home are stored in locked cabinets or carts in a locked room, accessible only to authorized staff, at the temperature on the label. Refrigerated items are kept in a locked, dedicated refrigerator with a temperature log. External and internal products are stored separately.

Controlled substances: Controlled substances are stored under double lock, counted at every shift change by two staff, and recorded in a perpetual count book, in line with State controlled substance regulations confirmed under the policy section. Any discrepancy is reported to the Administrator immediately and investigated.

Medication errors: Staff who find a medication error notify the nurse or Administrator immediately, check the resident, call the physician or 911 as needed, and complete an incident report under SAF-02 the same day. The Administrator reviews every error for cause and prevention.
Adverse reactions: Staff report any suspected reaction to the nurse and physician at once and follow RS-04.

Review: At least [monthly], the nurse or designated health professional reviews medication records and storage, and checks for expired, discontinued or unlabelled medications. Findings are given to the Administrator.

Disposal: Discontinued, expired or unused medications are removed from active storage, logged and held in locked storage until disposal. Disposal is done by two staff, or by [PHARMACY / DISPOSAL VENDOR], and recorded with date, drug, quantity, method and signatures. Controlled substances are disposed of in line with the controlled substance regulations. A resident's own medications are returned to the resident on discharge, with a signed receipt, unless the order has been discontinued.

Transfer and discharge: When a resident goes to hospital or is discharged, the nurse or medication staff send a current medication list and the medications as directed, and record what was sent (AD-06, RS-04).
Training: Staff are trained before assisting with medications, and annually after that, as ORI-02 and MED-02 explain.
Quality assurance: The Administrator includes medication errors, count discrepancies and audits in the quarterly review under GOV-02.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains and renews the Class 3A license, ensures compliance with 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d) and 10 NYCRR 1001.10, and reviews errors and audits.
Assesses self-administration ability, verifies orders, supervises storage and counts, audits records and oversees disposal.
Assist only within their authorization, record each assistance, and report errors and discrepancies.
Records the medication plan in the ISP and coordinates with physicians and pharmacies.

documentation: Class 3A limited controlled substance license and renewals
Self-administration assessments and ISP entries
Physician orders and medication lists
Medication assistance records, including PRN entries
Storage checks and refrigerator temperature logs
Controlled substance count books and discrepancy reports
Incident reports for medication errors
Disposal logs and discharge medication receipts
Monthly medication audits

policies.title: Medication Assistance, Staff Authorization and Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator, case manager, licensed nursing staff (RN/LPN), resident care aides and any other staff authorized to assist residents with medications; all residents who receive medication assistance
policies.purpose: To ensure that residents receive their medications safely, that staff assist only within the limits the State allows, and that every act of assistance, refusal and error is recorded and acted on.
policies.policy: This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 11 — Medication Management Policies and Procedures. [AGENCY NAME] supports each resident's right to self-administer medications when the resident is able. Where a resident needs help, only staff who have completed the required training and have been authorized in writing by the Administrator may assist, and only within the limits of 18 NYCRR 487.7(f) and 10 NYCRR 1001.10. Unlicensed staff do not give injections. Injectables are given only by licensed staff acting within their licensure. No staff member changes a dose, time, route or medication without written authorization from the resident's physician. Each resident who receives assistance has a medication assistance record, and PRN (as-needed) medications are handled under the PRN rules of 10 NYCRR 1001.10. Medication errors are reported on the Incident Report and the physician is notified. Storage, receipt, return and disposal are governed by MED-01. Applicant note on item 11: [AGENCY NAME] will apply for a Class 3A limited controlled substance license, timed just before the regional office on-site inspection, as the form directs (see procedure 14).

definitions.definition: The resident takes his or her own medication, with or without reminders, and is judged able to do so safely.

Help given by authorized, trained staff to a resident who directs his or her own medication use, limited to the activities allowed under 18 NYCRR 487.7(f) (for example reminding, bringing the labeled container to the resident, and observing).
Staff who have completed the medication training in ORI-02 and hold a current written authorization from the Administrator.
A registered nurse (RN) or licensed practical nurse (LPN) practicing within his or her scope of licensure.
A medication ordered by the physician to be taken only when needed, with written indication, dose and frequency.
The per-resident written record of each medication, dose, time, and the assistance given, refused or missed.
Any wrong resident, drug, dose, time, route or omission, or any assistance given outside this policy.

procedures: Before or at admission, the case manager and the resident's physician information (see AD-02) establish whether the resident can self-administer, needs reminders, or needs assistance. The decision and the physician's input are recorded in the ISP (AD-03).

The Administrator keeps a roster of authorized staff. A staff member is added only after completing the medication training in ORI-02 and being observed performing assistance correctly. The Administrator signs the written authorization and places it in the personnel record (PER-04).
Staff who are not on the authorized roster do not touch, open, hand out or remind residents about medications, except to call an authorized staff member or nurse.

Authorized staff assist only within the limits of 18 NYCRR 487.7(f). They check the resident's identity, read the pharmacy label and the physician's order, and give the resident the container or medication to take for himself or herself. They do not make clinical judgments about the need for a drug.

No unlicensed staff member gives an injection. Insulin and other injectables are self-administered by a resident who is able, or given by licensed staff (RN/LPN) where the resident is in the EALR or SNALR program and the service is within that program's approved scope (see EALR-01).

No staff member changes a dose, time, route or frequency, discontinues a drug or crushes a medication without written authorization from the physician. When a label and an order differ, staff stop and call the pharmacy or physician before assisting.

For every resident receiving assistance, authorized staff complete the medication assistance record at the time of assistance: resident, medication, dose, time, staff initials and signature, and any refusal or omission. Entries are never made in advance and corrections are made by a single line and initials.

PRN medications are assisted only under a current physician's order that states the reason for use, dose, frequency and maximum, and in accordance with the PRN rules in 10 NYCRR 1001.10. Staff do not decide on their own that a PRN is needed. The resident asks for it, or staff contact the physician or nurse for direction. Each PRN use, the reason and the result are recorded.

If a resident refuses a medication, staff do not force it. They record the refusal, tell the case manager the same shift, and the case manager notifies the physician as directed in RS-04. Repeated refusals are discussed at the ISP reassessment.
If a resident misses a dose, staff record it, contact the pharmacy or physician for instructions, and follow them. Staff never double a dose on their own.

Medication error response: staff (1) check the resident's condition, (2) call 911 if there is any serious reaction, (3) notify the physician or pharmacist for instructions, (4) notify the Administrator, and (5) complete an Incident Report before the end of the shift (SAF-02). The physician and the resident's representative are told of the error and the response is recorded.

In EALR and SNALR units, nursing services, including any injectable medication, are delivered by the RN or LPN assigned under the coverage requirements of 10 NYCRR 1001.11 (see EALR-01). Nurses document their medication services in the resident's record.

The Administrator checks the medication assistance records against pharmacy labels and orders at least monthly, reviews all error reports, and documents corrective action, retraining or removal of authorization when needed (GOV-02). Resident aides also receive the annual performance assessment with direct observation required by 10 NYCRR 1001.11, which includes medication assistance practices.

Controlled substances: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] will submit the application for a Class 3A limited controlled substance license to the appropriate authority just before the regional office's on-site inspection, as noted on DOH-5098 Schedule 6, item 11, and will keep a copy of the license on file. Residents' own controlled drugs are stored under double lock and counted per MED-01.
Medication assistance records and authorizations are kept as required in REC-01 and are available to the State surveyor on request.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes and removes staff, reviews records and errors monthly, applies for the Class 3A license, and ensures staff training is current.
Determines level of medication help at admission and reassessment, follows up on refusals and errors, and coordinates with physicians and pharmacy.
Gives injectables and other nursing medication services within licensure, and supervises medication practices on the unit.
Assist only within the allowed limits, complete the medication assistance record accurately, and report refusals and errors immediately.
Self-administers when able, tells staff of problems or changes, and may choose his or her own physician and pharmacy.

documentation: Written authorization and training record for each authorized staff member
Authorized staff roster
Medication assistance record for each resident
PRN log or PRN entries with reason and result
Physician orders and authorizations for any change
Incident Report for each medication error, with physician notification noted
Monthly record review and corrective action notes
Class 3A limited controlled substance license application and license

policies.title: EALR Skilled Nursing and Home Health Services, Nursing Coverage and Delegation
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN and LPN staff, advanced home health aides, resident care aides, case manager; all residents in the Enhanced Assisted Living Residence (EALR) program
policies.purpose: To describe the skilled nursing and home health aide services [AGENCY NAME] delivers directly with its own staff in the EALR program, how nursing coverage is staffed, and how tasks are assigned safely.
policies.policy: This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 13 — EALR Policies and Procedures. [AGENCY NAME] provides skilled nursing services, and home health aide services beyond what resident care aides may deliver, directly through its own staff only as listed in the EALR addendum. The list of services in this policy matches the EALR addendum. Any addition or deletion of an EALR service is made only after prior approval from the regional office. Nursing coverage meets 10 NYCRR 1001.11: an RN on site 8 hours a day, 5 days a week; an LPN on site 8 hours a day on the other 2 days; and an RN on call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. [AGENCY NAME] may request a waiver of the on-site minimum only if licensed at 40 or fewer beds. Aging in place under Public Health Law §4655 and the retention rules of 10 NYCRR 1001.10 apply to EALR residents, including the physician's report required for EALR retention. Immunization and TB records are kept for all EALR direct-care staff.

definitions.definition: An assisted living residence with Department approval under Public Health Law §4655 to allow residents to age in place with additional services.
A service performed by an RN or LPN within his or her licensure, as listed in the EALR addendum.
A home health aide who meets the advanced aide requirements of 10 NYCRR 1001.11 and performs tasks above the resident care aide scope.
An aide who has completed the initial training and annual in-service required by 10 NYCRR 1001.11.
The list of EALR services [AGENCY NAME] has submitted to and had approved by the Department.

procedures: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains the EALR service list, which names every skilled nursing service and every home health aide service above resident care aide scope that [AGENCY NAME] staff deliver: [LIST OF SERVICES AS STATED IN THE EALR ADDENDUM]. A written protocol exists for each listed service.

Each service protocol states who may perform the service (RN, LPN or advanced home health aide), the physician order required, how the resident is assessed beforehand, the steps, the monitoring, and where it is documented.

The Administrator compares the EALR service list to the EALR addendum at least annually and whenever a protocol is changed. Any service that is not in the addendum is not delivered by [AGENCY NAME] staff. Residents who need it are referred to an outside provider (a home care agency).

Before adding or deleting any EALR service, the Administrator submits a written request to the regional office and waits for written approval. The service list, protocols and training are updated only after approval is received.

Nursing schedules are built to provide an RN on site 8 hours a day for 5 days a week and an LPN on site 8 hours a day on the other 2 days. A named RN is on call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and the on-call RN's name and [PHONE] are posted at the nurse's station and given to the staff on duty each shift (STF-01).

If [AGENCY NAME] has 40 or fewer beds and wishes to rely on the waiver of the on-site minimum, the Administrator submits the waiver request to the Department and does not reduce on-site coverage until the waiver is granted in writing. Waiver conditions are kept in the administrative file.

The nurse on duty assigns tasks only to staff who are trained and qualified to perform them. Resident care aides do not perform tasks that are on the home health aide or nursing list. Tasks above resident care aide scope are assigned only to advanced home health aides who meet the requirements of 10 NYCRR 1001.11 and are supervised by the RN.

Before a resident receives any EALR service, the case manager and the RN confirm that the resident meets the EALR admission and retention conditions in AD-01 and 10 NYCRR 1001.10, including the physician's report required under Public Health Law §4655, and that the service is written in the ISP (AD-03).

The RN or LPN gives the service under a current physician order, documents each service in the resident's record the same shift, and reports a change in the resident's condition to the physician as directed in RS-04.
The RN supervises the nursing and aide staff on each shift and is available by phone to staff at all times. Medication-related nursing duties are carried out as described in MED-02.

Before starting work, every direct-care staff member in the EALR has immunization and TB records on file as required by 10 NYCRR 1001.11 (PER-03). The Administrator does not schedule direct-care staff without these records.

If the nursing schedule cannot be met on any day (for example, because of illness), the Administrator arranges a qualified replacement the same day, records the gap and the response, and does not accept new EALR admissions until coverage is restored.

When a resident's needs exceed what [AGENCY NAME] is approved to provide, the case manager follows discharge and transfer procedures in AD-06 and the retention rules of 10 NYCRR 1001.10, working with the resident, family, physician and hospice or home health provider (RS-06).
The Administrator reviews EALR services, coverage records and incident reports quarterly as part of quality assurance (GOV-02) and records the findings.

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the EALR service list matched to the addendum, obtains approvals for changes, requests any waiver, and ensures coverage and staff records.
Provides skilled nursing, supervises LPNs and aides, is on site and on call as scheduled, and assigns tasks by qualification.
Provides nursing services within licensure, under RN supervision, on the days assigned.

responsibilities.role: Advanced home health aide / resident care aide
responsibilities.duty: Performs only tasks within his or her trained and approved scope.
Coordinates ISP and retention decisions and physician reports for EALR residents.

documentation: EALR service list matched to the EALR addendum
Service protocols
Regional office approvals for additions and deletions
Nursing schedules and on-call roster
Waiver request and decision, if applicable
Immunization and TB records for direct-care staff
Physician's report and orders for each EALR resident
Nursing service notes
Quarterly review notes

policies.title: SNALR Dementia Unit Plan, Memory Care and Wandering Safeguards
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN/LPN staff, unit staff, case manager, activities director; all residents admitted to the Special Needs Assisted Living Residence (SNALR) dementia unit and their families
policies.purpose: To state the plan under which [AGENCY NAME] operates its dementia unit, so residents with dementia receive appropriate care in a safe environment.
policies.policy: This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 14a — SNALR Policies and Procedures: the dementia unit/SNALR plan. [AGENCY NAME] submits its dementia unit/SNALR plan following the Department's published SNALR plan guide. The SNALR beds are located in a fixed, identified area of the building as required by 10 NYCRR 1001.13. The plan addresses unit staffing, dementia-specific training, the physical environment, wandering safeguards (SAF-02), activities (SNALR-02) and the family organization (ORG-01). Nursing coverage on the unit is the same as for the EALR under 10 NYCRR 1001.11: RN on site 8 hours a day, 5 days a week; LPN 8 hours a day on the other 2 days; RN on call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

definitions.definition: A Special Needs Assisted Living Residence approved to care for residents with moderate to severe cognitive impairment, including dementia, in a designated unit.
The fixed, designated area of the building where SNALR beds are located.
A resident's walking about or leaving a safe area without awareness of danger or ability to return.
The written plan submitted to the Department that describes how the unit operates, in the form set out in the Department's SNALR plan guide.

procedures: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] prepares the dementia unit/SNALR plan using the Department's current SNALR plan guide and submits it with Schedule 6. The plan is reviewed at least annually and whenever the unit changes.

The plan identifies the SNALR beds by room number on a floor plan and shows that they are in a fixed area of the building (10 NYCRR 1001.13). Beds are not moved into or out of the unit without prior notice to, and approval from, the regional office.

The plan states the unit's admission and retention criteria, consistent with AD-01, and describes the pre-admission evaluation by the case manager and a physician's input (AD-02). Residents are admitted only when the evaluation supports the unit as appropriate.

Staffing: the plan shows the number and type of staff on each shift on the unit, consistent with STF-01, and the RN/LPN/on-call RN coverage required by 10 NYCRR 1001.11. At least one staff member is on the unit at all times when residents are present.

Training: every staff member who works on the unit completes dementia-specific training before working alone on the unit and annually thereafter, in the amount and content required by the Department's SNALR plan guide. Training is recorded in the personnel file (ORI-02, PER-04).

Care approach: each resident has an ISP that addresses cognition, behaviors, communication, safety, nutrition, toileting, sleep and family involvement (AD-03). Staff use non-drug approaches first for behavioral symptoms and do not use physical restraints (SAF-03).

Environment: the plan describes how the unit is kept safe and calm, including secured exits or alarms, clear sightlines, safe outdoor access, lighting, signage, and removal of hazards. The Administrator inspects the unit weekly and records findings (HK-01).

Wandering safeguards: residents at risk are identified at admission and at every reassessment and listed on a current at-risk roster. A recent photograph and description are kept for each at-risk resident. Alarm or door-control devices are tested at least weekly, and a failure is repaired or covered by additional staff supervision immediately. If a resident is missing, staff follow the missing resident and elopement steps in SAF-02 without delay.
Activities: the unit offers a daily activities schedule designed for residents' cognitive abilities (SNALR-02).

Family: the plan provides for a family organization and regular communication with families about each resident's condition and the unit program (ORG-01). Families are told in the admission agreement what the unit offers (AD-05).
Change in condition and transfers: staff follow RS-04. When a resident can no longer be safely cared for on the unit, the case manager follows AD-06 and the retention rules of 10 NYCRR 1001.10.
The Administrator reviews unit incidents, falls, elopement attempts and use of any safeguards at least quarterly and revises the plan or staffing as needed (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and submits the plan, keeps it current, ensures staffing and training, and notifies the regional office of changes.
Provides the required nursing coverage on the unit and oversees resident health and behavior care.
Evaluates for admission, writes ISPs, maintains the wandering-risk roster, and works with families.
Complete dementia training, supervise residents, test safeguards as assigned and report concerns immediately.
Develops the unit activities schedule and records participation.

documentation: Dementia unit/SNALR plan and floor plan showing the fixed unit area
Staffing and nursing coverage schedules
Dementia training records
Wandering-risk roster with photographs
Alarm and door device test log
Weekly unit environment inspection record
Unit incident review notes
ISPs for unit residents

policies.title: SNALR Activities Schedule
policies.applies_to: Activities director, unit staff, case manager, Administrator; all residents of the SNALR dementia unit
policies.purpose: To make sure that residents of the dementia unit have meaningful activities each day that match their cognitive abilities and that participation is recorded.
policies.policy: This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 14b — SNALR Policies and Procedures: the dementia unit/SNALR activities schedule. [AGENCY NAME] submits a dementia unit/SNALR activities schedule with Schedule 6. Activities fit residents' cognitive abilities and are offered every day, including evenings and weekends. Activities are staffed, participation is recorded, and the schedule is reviewed at least quarterly. This policy supports the SNALR services required under 10 NYCRR 1001.10 and the unit plan in SNALR-01 and applies to the unit identified under 10 NYCRR 1001.13.

definitions.definition: The written weekly calendar of planned activities on the dementia unit, showing time, activity, location, staff responsible and the ability levels it serves.
An activity that residents can take part in successfully at their current level of memory, attention, communication and physical ability.

procedures: The activities director prepares a weekly activities schedule for the unit and posts it in the unit's common area in large, easy-to-read print. A copy is sent with Schedule 6.
The schedule offers activities every day of the week, including at least one planned activity in the evening and on each weekend day. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] verifies this before approving the schedule.

The activities director builds the schedule from each resident's life history, interests, abilities and preferences, collected at admission by the case manager (AD-02) and recorded in the ISP (AD-03). Examples include music, reminiscence, exercise and movement, sensory and craft activities, gardening, and supervised outdoor time.
The schedule includes activities for different ability levels, including individual or small-group options for residents who cannot join large groups or who are in bed or in their rooms.

Each activity has a named staff member responsible. Unit staff are assigned to support activities so that supervision of the unit is not reduced (STF-01). Staff who lead activities are trained in dementia care (SNALR-01).
Residents are invited, encouraged and helped to take part but are not forced. Declined activities are respected and alternatives are offered (RS-02).

Staff record each activity on an attendance sheet: date, activity, staff, residents who took part, and a brief note on response. Residents who repeatedly decline or do not take part are reported to the case manager.
The case manager reviews participation at each ISP review and adjusts the plan for residents who are not engaged (AD-03).

The activities director and Administrator review the schedule and the participation records at least quarterly, with input from residents, families and staff, and revise the schedule as needed. The review is dated and signed.
Any change to the posted schedule on a given day is posted before the change is made. Cancelled activities are replaced with an alternative the same day.
Records are kept as required in REC-01 and are available to the State surveyor.

responsibilities.duty: Writes, posts and updates the schedule, leads or assigns activities, and keeps participation records.
Help residents attend, lead assigned activities and record participation.
Provides resident interest information and reviews participation in the ISP.
Approves the schedule, checks daily, evening and weekend coverage, and signs the quarterly review.

documentation: Weekly dementia unit activities schedule (submitted with Schedule 6)
Activity attendance and participation sheets
Resident interest information in the ISP
Quarterly schedule review record, signed and dated

policies.title: ALP Referral Sources, Co-located Beds and Site Description
policies.applies_to: Administrator, ALP designated individual, case manager; the Assisted Living Program (ALP) and its referral and discharge partners
policies.purpose: To describe where the ALP's residents come from and go to, how the ALP relates to other programs in the building, and the site and its access to community services, as required for a newly established ALP.
policies.policy: This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Schedule 6, item 15a — ALP referral and discharge sources and relationships; item 15b — relationship of the ALP to any non-ALP adult home or enriched housing beds in the same building; and item 15c — the proposed ALP site and its access to community services. The ALP is established under Social Services Law §461-l, which requires a licensed home care services agency (LHCSA) or certified home health agency (CHHA) under identical ownership, and Public Health and Health Planning Council (PHHPC) approval of a new LHCSA. New ALP beds are approved case by case on the basis of public need from April 1, 2025. ALP services are delivered as described in 18 NYCRR 494.5 and ALP-02. The ALP application forms part of the Part II program review described in 18 NYCRR 485.6.

definitions.definition: The Medicaid Assisted Living Program under Social Services Law §461-l, for eligible residents who would otherwise need nursing home placement.
An organization or person that sends residents to the ALP (for example, a hospital, county social services, a nursing home, a community agency or a physician).
A setting or provider to which an ALP resident goes after leaving the ALP.
Non-ALP adult home or enriched housing beds in the same building as the ALP.

procedures: 15a — Referral and discharge sources. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps a written list of anticipated referral sources and discharge destinations, and the relationship planned with each: [LIST HOSPITALS, COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES, NURSING HOMES, HOME CARE AND HOSPICE PROVIDERS, PHYSICIANS AND COMMUNITY AGENCIES]. The list is submitted with Schedule 6.

For each referral source, the Administrator states in writing how referrals will be received (named contact, [PHONE] and process), what information the source will send, and how [AGENCY NAME] will report back to the source on the outcome of the referral.

For each discharge destination, the Administrator states the planned relationship, such as transfer agreements, hospital discharge planning contacts, and arrangements for return to the community or to a nursing home, and ties the arrangements to AD-06.

All referrals are evaluated using the admission and retention standards in AD-01 and the pre-admission evaluation in AD-02. Referral relationships do not change the standards or the resident's right to choose providers (RS-02).

15b — Co-located beds. The Administrator answers whether the ALP will be in the same building as non-ALP adult home or enriched housing beds: [YES/NO]. If yes, the Administrator describes in writing how the ALP relates to those programs: which floors, wings or rooms are ALP beds and which are not; how ALP residents are identified; how ALP services and staff are kept separate and distinct from the adult home or enriched housing program for admission, services, staffing, billing and records; and what shared spaces and services residents of both programs use.

Where the programs share a building, the Administrator keeps a floor plan marked to show ALP beds and verifies each month that ALP residents occupy ALP beds and that Medicaid capitated services are billed only for ALP residents (ALP-02).
Admission agreements and residents' notices state which program the resident is in and what services the resident will receive (AD-05).

15c — Site and access. The Administrator prepares a written description of the proposed ALP site, including address [ADDRESS], the building and grounds, the number and type of ALP beds, accessibility, and the physical relationship to community services. The description covers the distance to and access to hospitals, physicians, pharmacies, public transportation, shopping, faith communities, and recreation and senior services in the area.
The Administrator describes how residents will reach community services, including transportation provided or arranged by [AGENCY NAME] (OPT-01), and how the ALP will support residents' use of them.

The Administrator confirms and documents the ownership and approval conditions in SSL §461-l: the LHCSA or CHHA under identical ownership, PHHPC approval for a new LHCSA, and the public need review for new ALP beds, and keeps the application file, correspondence and approvals together in the administrative record.

The Administrator reviews this description at least annually and whenever a referral relationship, the building layout or the bed count changes, and tells the regional office of material changes before they are made (GOV-01).
Copies of this policy, the lists and the site description are kept in the administrative file and are available to the regional office during the Part II review and the pre-opening inspection.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and keeps current the referral, discharge, co-location and site descriptions and ensures compliance with the ALP approval conditions.
Maintains referral and discharge relationships and the working contacts with each source.
Evaluates referrals against admission standards and reports outcomes to referral sources.
Approves the program description and any material change.

documentation: List of referral sources and discharge destinations, with planned relationships
Written description of the relationship between the ALP and any non-ALP beds
Floor plan marking ALP beds
Site description with access to community services
ALP approval file: LHCSA or CHHA ownership, PHHPC approval, public need review correspondence
Referral and discharge logs

policies.title: ALP Services, Capitated Rate and Medicaid Compliance
policies.applies_to: Administrator, ALP designated individual, case manager, billing and administrative staff, all staff and contractors who work in the ALP
policies.purpose: To make sure that the Assisted Living Program provides the services covered by the Medicaid capitated rate, is properly staffed, bills correctly, and complies with Medicaid program integrity requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides ALP services as defined in 18 NYCRR 494.5 and staffs the ALP as required by 18 NYCRR 494.6, including a designated individual, a qualified case manager, and the minimum staffing levels of 18 NYCRR 487.9(f)(6). The Medicaid capitated rate is set by the Department at 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by wage-equalization region under Public Health Law §3614(6), and [AGENCY NAME] does not bill residents for services covered by the rate. Residents enrolled in the ALP are not eligible for managed long term care (MLTC) under Public Health Law §4403-f. The ALP operates under Social Services Law §461-l. [AGENCY NAME] maintains a compliance program under Social Services Law §363-d and 18 NYCRR Part 521 (applicability thresholds to be confirmed by the Administrator with counsel), complies with the federal False Claims Act (31 USC 3729), and screens staff and contractors against federal exclusion (42 USC 1320a-7). This policy has no separate item on the DOH-5098 Schedule 6 checklist and supports item 15.

definitions.definition: The fixed daily Medicaid payment per eligible ALP resident covering the services listed in 18 NYCRR 494.5.
The person named under 18 NYCRR 494.6 as responsible for the ALP.
A case manager who meets the qualifications for the ALP under 18 NYCRR 494.6 (see QUAL-01).
A person or entity excluded from participation in federal health care programs under 42 USC 1320a-7.
A claim for payment that is false or fraudulent, including billing for services not provided, under 31 USC 3729.

procedures: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps a current list of the services included in the capitated rate according to 18 NYCRR 494.5 and ensures that each is available to every ALP resident when needed, either by [AGENCY NAME] staff or through the affiliated LHCSA or CHHA. The list is given to residents and referral sources and is part of the admission agreement (AD-05).

The ALP resident's need for each service is determined at pre-admission evaluation (AD-02) and recorded in the ISP (AD-03). Services are delivered as written in the ISP, and delivery is recorded on the day it occurs.

The governing body names a designated individual for the ALP and a qualified case manager (QUAL-01) and keeps proof of qualifications and hours in the personnel records. The Administrator confirms that staffing meets 18 NYCRR 494.6 and the minimum levels in 18 NYCRR 487.9(f)(6), and reports any shortfall to the governing body the same day (STF-01).

The ALP maintains the LHCSA or CHHA under identical ownership and the PHHPC approval required by Social Services Law §461-l. The Administrator keeps the license and approvals current and tells the regional office of any change in ownership or license status before it takes effect (GOV-01).

Rates: the Medicaid capitated rate is set by the Department using the methodology of Public Health Law §3614(6). The Administrator keeps the rate notices received and sends rate questions in writing to ALP-Rates@health.ny.gov. [AGENCY NAME] does not set or change the rate on its own.

Billing staff bill only for eligible, enrolled ALP residents, for the days the resident is actually in the ALP, and at the rate notified by the Department. Claims are reviewed against the resident roster and attendance each month by someone other than the person who prepared them. Discrepancies are corrected and recorded before the claim is submitted, and any overpayment is reported and returned as the Department directs.
Residents are not asked to pay separately for services covered by the capitated rate. Any charge for services outside the rate is stated in the admission agreement and is lawful (AD-05, FUN-01).

Staff do not enroll an ALP resident in MLTC or ask the resident to do so, because ALP residents are not eligible for MLTC under Public Health Law §4403-f. If a resident wishes to move to MLTC, the case manager explains the need to leave the ALP and handles the change as a discharge or transfer (AD-06).

Compliance program: the Administrator confirms with counsel whether Social Services Law §363-d and 18 NYCRR Part 521 apply to [AGENCY NAME], based on the thresholds in the rule, and records the determination in writing. If applicable, [AGENCY NAME] adopts the required compliance program elements and names a compliance officer, [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME]. Even if the thresholds are not met, [AGENCY NAME] follows this policy as its standard.

Training: all ALP staff receive training at hire and annually on this policy, the False Claims Act (31 USC 3729), accurate documentation and billing, and how to report concerns. Attendance is recorded (ORI-01, ORI-02).

Exclusion screening: before hire or contract, and at least monthly afterward, the Administrator checks every employee, volunteer and contractor against the federal exclusion lists, including individuals excluded under 42 USC 1320a-7, and against the State lists, as described in PER-02. An excluded person is not hired or retained, and no claims include services ordered or provided by an excluded person.

Reporting concerns: any staff member who believes a claim, record or practice is false or improper reports it to the Administrator or compliance officer, or to the governing body if the concern involves the Administrator. Retaliation against a person who reports in good faith is prohibited (PER-01). Reports are investigated promptly and the outcome and corrective action are recorded.

Records that support services and billing (ISPs, service delivery records, attendance, claims and rate notices) are kept as required in REC-01 and made available to the Department and Medicaid program staff on request.
The Administrator reviews ALP staffing, service delivery, billing accuracy and compliance activities quarterly with the governing body and records the results and any corrective action (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Names the designated individual, approves this policy, and reviews compliance and staffing reports quarterly.
Ensures covered services are delivered, staffing meets requirements, billing is accurate, rate questions go to the Department, and exclusion screening is done.
Oversees ALP operations and staffing as required by 18 NYCRR 494.6.
Determines service needs, writes ISPs, tracks service delivery and explains MLTC ineligibility to residents.
Prepare claims from verified rosters and attendance and correct errors before submission.
Runs the compliance program, receives reports and tracks corrective action.
Document services accurately and report suspected improper claims or practices.

ISPs and service delivery records

policies.title: Personnel Policies: Rules of Conduct, Hiring, Termination, Employee Grievances and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, including full-time, part-time, per-diem and agency/contract staff, and resident volunteers and resident employees where applicable. Applies to the [AGENCY NAME] Adult Home / Enriched Housing Program, its Assisted Living Residence (ALR, EALR, SNALR) and, if licensed, its Assisted Living Program (ALP).
policies.purpose: To set out the written rules of conduct, hiring practices, termination practices, employee grievance procedure and professional boundary rules that keep residents safe and respected, keep staffing stable, and treat employees fairly and lawfully.
policies.policy: This policy meets DOH-5098 (1/26) Sched. 6, item 17 — Personnel Policies and Procedures, which requires rules of conduct, the facility policy on grievance procedures, and hiring and termination policies. Each element is addressed below: (1) Rules of Conduct (Procedures 1-6 and 14); (2) Employee Grievance Procedure (Procedures 11-13); (3) Hiring Policy (Procedures 7-10); and (4) Termination Policy (Procedures 14-17). [AGENCY NAME] hires only people who can speak, read and write English, as required by 18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(13), and who meet the qualifications, health and background requirements in PER-02, PER-03 and JD-01. Where the facility is subject to the Justice Center, every employee must follow the Justice Center code of conduct, and it is part of these rules of conduct. Residents who volunteer or are employed are governed by 18 NYCRR §487.9(b): participation is voluntary, never counts toward required staffing, and is never a condition of admission or retention. [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate against applicants or employees on a basis prohibited by law and provides reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities in line with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101). Staff may not accept gifts, loans or tips from residents or their families. They may not enter into financial dealings or personal, romantic or sexual relationships with residents. No employee may retaliate against any person who reports a concern in good faith.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates an employee's professional role from a personal, financial or social relationship with a resident or the resident's family.
The written standards of behavior all employees must follow, with the disciplinary steps that apply when they are broken.
A work-related complaint raised by an employee about working conditions, treatment, discipline or the application of agency policy.
A vacancy in a position for which 18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(16) requires notice to the DOH regional office within 3 business days (e.g., the administrator or other key position, as identified in QUAL-01).
The NYS Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs, to which reportable incidents are made where the facility is subject to its jurisdiction.

procedures: The Administrator issues the written Rules of Conduct to every employee at hire during general orientation (ORI-01). The employee signs an acknowledgment, and HR files it in the personnel record (PER-04).

Rules of Conduct require employees to: treat residents with dignity and courtesy; honor resident rights (RS-02); report abuse, neglect, exploitation or mistreatment immediately (SAF-01); protect resident confidentiality (RS-07); arrive on time and follow the posted schedule; and never work impaired by alcohol, drugs or illness that endangers residents.

Professional boundaries: employees may not accept gifts, money, tips, loans, bequests or favors from residents, families or representatives; may not borrow from, lend to, buy from, sell to or manage money for residents (except through the resident fund process in FUN-01 by authorized staff); and may not enter into personal, romantic or sexual relationships with residents. An employee who is offered a gift politely declines it and reports the offer to the Administrator the same day.

Employees may not use residents' property, phones or accounts, may not give personal contact information to residents for non-work purposes, and may not post resident information or images on social media or personal devices.

Where the facility is subject to the Justice Center, the Administrator gives each employee the Justice Center code of conduct at orientation, and the employee signs that it was received and explained.

Resident volunteers and resident employees: the Administrator may allow a resident to volunteer or work only if the resident asks to do so freely, the activity is documented in the resident's record, and it is consistent with the resident's ISP (AD-03). Residents are never used to meet required staffing, and any paid work follows applicable wage rules (WC-01) and the standards of 18 NYCRR §487.9(b).

Hiring step 1: the Administrator approves each open position against the job description (JD-01) and posts it. Hiring decisions are based on qualifications, experience, references and legal eligibility only.

Hiring step 2: HR collects a signed application, verifies identity and work eligibility (Form I-9), and confirms the applicant can speak, read and write English (18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(13)) through a short interview and a brief written task. Licenses, certificates and training (e.g., HHA, first aid, LPN/RN) are verified at the source and copied to the file.

Hiring step 3: before any unsupervised resident contact, HR completes background checks and registry checks (PER-02) and the pre-employment health statement and TB assessment (PER-03). The Administrator signs an offer only after all clearances are in the file.

Hiring step 4: new hires receive a written job description, the Rules of Conduct, the employee grievance procedure, and orientation and training per ORI-01 and ORI-02. The Administrator documents the start date and completion of each item.

Employee grievance step 1: an employee who has a work-related complaint raises it with the immediate supervisor, orally or in writing, within 30 days of the event. The supervisor responds within 5 business days.

Employee grievance step 2: if the matter is not resolved, the employee may submit a written grievance to the Administrator, who meets with the employee and issues a written decision within 10 business days. If the grievance concerns the Administrator, the employee may take it directly to [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT].

Employee grievance step 3: the employee may appeal to the governing body (GOV-01) in writing within 10 business days of the Administrator's decision. The governing body's decision is final and documented. No employee is retaliated against for filing a grievance. Reports of abuse, neglect or resident safety concerns are never delayed by the grievance process and are handled under SAF-01.

Discipline: the Administrator uses progressive discipline (verbal warning, written warning, suspension, termination) in proportion to the conduct. Conduct such as abuse, neglect, theft, resident exploitation, working impaired, falsifying records or boundary violations may result in immediate suspension and termination. Where required, the Administrator ensures a Justice Center report has been made.

Termination (voluntary): employees give at least two weeks' written notice where possible. Termination (involuntary): the Administrator and a second manager meet with the employee, state the reason in writing, and collect keys, badges, uniforms and agency property the same day.

Final pay and records: HR pays final wages by the next regular payday, documents an exit checklist (access removed, keys returned, medication-authorization status ended), and files the separation notice in the personnel record (PER-04).

Key vacancies: when a key position becomes vacant, the Administrator notifies the DOH regional office within 3 business days (18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(16)) and designates coverage per QUAL-01 and STF-01. Notice is documented, with the date and the name of the person notified.
The Administrator reviews these personnel policies at least annually with the governing body, updates them as the law or program changes, and re-issues them to all employees.

responsibilities.duty: Approves hires and terminations, enforces the Rules of Conduct, hears grievances, makes vacancy notices to the DOH regional office, and reviews the policy annually.
Verifies credentials and English proficiency, completes clearances, issues policies, and maintains personnel records.

Follow the rules of conduct and professional boundaries, report violations and abuse, and sign acknowledgments.
Hears final employee grievance appeals and approves personnel policies.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of Rules of Conduct, boundary rules and (if applicable) Justice Center code of conduct.
Application, I-9, English proficiency documentation, credential verifications and reference checks.

Written grievances, responses, decisions and appeal results.
Disciplinary records and counseling notes.

Annual policy review sign-off.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: All applicants and employees, including direct-care staff, agency/contract staff, and volunteers who have unsupervised access to residents; ALP/Medicaid-funded staff for the federal exclusion checks.
policies.purpose: To ensure no person who is barred, excluded or unsuitable has contact with residents, by running criminal history record checks and required registry and exclusion-list checks before hire and on a regular schedule afterward.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] runs a criminal history record check for every direct-care employee as required by 18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(7). Where the facility is subject to the Justice Center, it checks the Justice Center Staff Exclusion List and the State Central Register before hire, as required by 18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(17). For ALP and other Medicaid-funded staff, [AGENCY NAME] also checks the federal exclusion lists, consistent with the exclusion authority in 42 USC 1320a-7. No person on an exclusion list, and no person whose check has not cleared, may work in a resident-care role. Results are filed in the personnel record. All checks are repeated on a schedule of at least annually, and federal exclusion lists are checked monthly. Where a reportable incident is alleged, the facility meets its duty to report immediately to the Justice Center and starts an investigation as required by 18 NYCRR §487.14.

definitions.definition: A fingerprint-based check of state and federal criminal history conducted through the process required by DOH for adult care facility employees.
The list of individuals barred from employment in facilities subject to the Justice Center because of substantiated findings.
The Justice Center register of reports of abuse and neglect; checks are made as required for facilities subject to the Justice Center.
The HHS-OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE), the federal SAM.gov exclusion database and the NYS OMIG exclusion list, used to confirm a person may be paid with Medicaid funds.

procedures: The Administrator designates [BACKGROUND CHECK DESIGNEE] as responsible for all background and registry checks, with the Administrator as backup.
At the offer stage, the designee obtains the applicant's signed consent and disclosure forms and gives fingerprinting instructions for the criminal history record check.
The applicant completes fingerprinting before the start date. The designee tracks the request and records the date submitted and the date results are received.

Before the first shift, and before any unsupervised resident contact, the designee checks the Justice Center Staff Exclusion List and the State Central Register where the facility is subject to the Justice Center (18 NYCRR §487.9(a)(17)).

For ALP and other Medicaid-funded positions, the designee also searches the HHS-OIG LEIE, SAM.gov and the NYS OMIG exclusion list, and for home health aides checks the NYS Home Care Registry. The designee prints or saves the dated screen showing the result.
If any result is a hit or is pending, the employee does not work in a resident-care role. The designee notifies the Administrator the same day.

If a criminal history result shows a conviction or open charge, the Administrator reviews it with counsel or DOH guidance, considers the nature of the offense, time passed and relation to the job and resident safety, and documents the decision in writing. Anyone barred by law is not employed.
Any applicant or employee on the Justice Center Staff Exclusion List, or on a federal exclusion list, is not hired or is removed from duty immediately and terminated per PER-01.

The designee reviews results and signs and dates a Background Clearance Checklist for each employee. It is filed in the personnel record (PER-04) and the Administrator countersigns it before the employee is added to the schedule.
Monthly, the designee re-screens all ALP/Medicaid-funded staff against the federal exclusion lists and records the date of each screening.

At least annually, on each employee's anniversary or on a fixed date set by the Administrator, the designee re-checks the Justice Center Staff Exclusion List and the registries used at hire, and records the date.

Employees must tell the Administrator within 2 business days if they are arrested for, charged with, or convicted of any offense, or are named in an abuse or neglect report. The Administrator decides on duty status within 1 business day and documents it.

When a reportable incident is alleged against an employee at a facility subject to the Justice Center, any mandated reporter reports it to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause, and the Administrator starts an investigation (18 NYCRR §487.14) and follows SAF-01. The employee is removed from resident contact as the investigation requires.

Contract and agency staff and volunteers with unsupervised access: the Administrator obtains written proof from the agency or vendor that equivalent checks were done, or runs the checks directly, before the person works.
The Administrator reviews the checklist log quarterly to confirm there are no overdue re-checks, and reports exceptions to the governing body (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the designee, makes final decisions on adverse results, countersigns clearances and ensures reporting to the Justice Center.
Runs and documents all initial, monthly and annual checks and tracks pending items.
Cooperate with checks and promptly disclose arrests, charges and convictions.
Receives quarterly exception reports.

documentation: Signed consent and disclosure forms.
Criminal history record check results and decision notes.
Dated screenshots or printouts of Staff Exclusion List, SCR, federal exclusion list and registry checks.
